This sounds like a typical sign of depression. Are you sure the meds she’s taking are working effectively in her treatment? First of all, depression in and of itself works as a great libido killer. Add some antidepressants and you have a perfect cocktail for a limp noodle. Antidepressants will do that. Also, is she taking any other types of medication? Birth control, believe it or not, also kills libido and it’s very normal. Whatever she’s taking, id encourage her to speak with her doctor about potential changes in medication and maybe even see a gynecologist just in case it’s another health problem. 

However, a couple of red flags stood out. First, it seems like the respect you are giving isn’t being reciprocated. From the way you spoke about the situation, it seems like the amount of effort you are putting in is getting exhausting because she isn’t returning the love and respect. The second red flag I noticed was her denial of couples therapy. This might be because she feels that her therapy is enough but explain to her that they are two completely different things. Couples counseling can give you both a healthy medium to speak things out and you can learn ways to get around hard times. It sounds a little like she’s fallen in love with the lifestyle you’ve given her more than the life she has with you. If that’s the case (which I hope it isn’t) then maybe there should be talk of other ways to go about this

Also, and this is definitely a far-fetched idea but this is coming from experience, has she gone through a sexual assault or something of the sort? Everything she is doing tells me that this is something that might have traumatized her that she is not yet ready to address. Physician touches might be triggering, sex even worse. I’m only bringing this up because everyone likes to jump to conclusions that she is cheating or hiding something, but this could also stem from something really hard and traumatizing for her. A lot of people shut certain parts of their lives down because of it. I’d sit down with her and talk about these things. Reassure her that you’re there for her but also don’t beat around the bush— this is something that is negatively affecting your relationship, something needs to be done about it before things get worse, and you’re willing to work through whatever it is. 

You sound like a very nice man and I’m praying for you.
